parsedVerdict.reasoning: All five files are order and stock use cases, which is one cohesive application concern. Each reaches persistence only through the domain ports OrderRepository and ProductRepository, plus the StockManager domain service. No file uses a database, ORM or query client directly. The non-empty-lines rule is defined once, as assertExecuteRule in PlaceOrderUseCase.ts. ListOrdersByStatusUseCase imports and calls it rather than copying it, so this is not duplication. The order-to-DTO object is built inline in four files. That is repeated mapping code, not a duplicated business rule or invariant, so it does not fail the rubric. ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.validateExecute validates a CreateOrderRequest, which is out of place in a listing use case. It delegates to the shared rule, so I treat it as a smell rather than a split concern. UpdateOrderStatusUseCase hard-codes a validStatuses list, and PlaceOrderUseCase checks for quantity <= 0. Either might repeat checks in Order.ts (the OrderStatus type or transitionTo), but that file is not in the material provided, so I cannot confirm a duplicate.
